description: Both chorine and water softener need to be added to a pool. One unit of chlorine takes 1 minute to be effective while one unit of water softener takes 2 minutes to be effective. Because too much chlorine can burn your eyes, there has to at most half as much chlorine as water softener in the pool. If there has to be at least 200 units of chlorine in the water and a total of 500 units of chemicals in the water, how many units of each should be added to minimize the total time it takes for the pool to be ready? (Note: chlorine must be added before water softener or vice versa).

ChlorineEffectivenessTime.definition: The time in minutes for one unit of chlorine to become effective

WaterSoftenerEffectivenessTime.definition: The time in minutes for one unit of water softener to become effective

MaxChlorineToWaterSoftenerRatio.definition: The maximum allowed ratio of chlorine to water softener in the pool

MinChlorineUnits.definition: The minimum required units of chlorine to be added to the pool

TotalChemicalUnits.definition: The total number of chemical units to be added to the pool

objective.description: "Minimize the total time required for the pool to be ready (i.e., the total time until the added chlorine and water softener become effective)."

constraints.description: The amount of chlorine added must be at most half the amount of water softener added (Chlorine ≤ 0.5 × WaterSoftener)
The amount of chlorine added must be at least 200 units (Chlorine ≥ 200)
The total amount of chemicals added must equal 500 units (Chlorine + WaterSoftener = 500)
